title: Turnkey Repower of Motor Yacht Fair Winds
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice only. The solicitation is not available at this time, and proposals submitted in response to this notice will not be accepted. The U.S. Embassy Singapore intends to issue a solicitation for the turnkey repower of the U.S. Government-owned Motor Yacht Fair Winds, a 51-foot motor yacht located in Singapore. The solicitation will include the complete Statement of Work, submission requirements, evaluation criteria, and applicable terms and conditions. The anticipated requirement includes removal of two existing Caterpillar C12 marine diesel engines and the furnishing, installation, testing, and commissioning of two new Cummins QSM11-M 715 HO marine diesel engines. The work is anticipated to include, but is not limited to, vessel haul-out, pressure washing, and hard-stand services; removal and restoration of the engine hatch, teak decking, and other components necessary to access the machinery space; removal of the existing engines; inspection and evaluation of the existing marine gearboxes; installation of new engine mounts; integration of mechanical, fuel, cooling, exhaust, electrical, electronic-control, and navigation systems; alignment; dockside operational testing; sea trials; commissioning; and restoration of disturbed vessel structures and finishes. The contractor will be required to inspect the existing marine gearboxes and submit a written gearbox inspection and compatibility report. The report shall document the condition, compatibility, estimated remaining useful life, identified deficiencies, and recommended disposition of each existing gearbox. If the existing gearboxes are determined to be compatible, serviceable, and suitable for continued operation, the contractor shall connect and integrate them with the new engines and complete the required alignment, testing, sea trials, and commissioning. The purchase, furnishing, replacement, rebuilding, overhaul, modification, or installation of replacement marine gearboxes will not be included in the anticipated Firm-Fixed-Price requirement. If either existing gearbox is determined to be incompatible, unserviceable, or unsuitable for continued operation, the contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer immediately and shall not proceed with the affected work without written direction from the Contracting Officer. The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed-Price contract. The Government may award the contract based on initial proposals without conducting discussions. A vessel inspection, site visit, and preproposal conference are anticipated. The date, time, location, registration procedures, security requirements, and access instructions will be provided in the solicitation. The solicitation and any amendments will be posted electronically on SAM.gov. The solicitation posting date has not yet been established. The Government will not provide individual notification when the solicitation or any amendment is posted, and paper copies will not be provided. Offerors must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management at https://www.sam.gov when submitting an offer and at the time of contract award. SAM registration is free. Prospective offerors are encouraged to begin the registration process early because registration may take several weeks to complete. Registration assistance is available through the Federal Service Desk at https://www.fsd.gov. All contract performance will take place in Singapore. The contractor must have access to a qualified marine repair facility in Singapore capable of safely accommodating a 51-foot motor yacht and performing the required lifting, engine removal, installation, integration, testing, and commissioning services. Because contract performance will take place in Singapore, the contractor, including any subcontractor or joint-venture partner that will perform the work, must be legally authorized to operate and conduct business in Singapore. The contractor and each performing subcontractor or joint-venture partner must possess all licenses, permits, registrations, approvals, and professional or technical qualifications required to perform the work in Singapore. The solicitation will include Department of State Acquisition Regulation clause 652.242-73, Authorization and Performance (AUG 1999). title: SCBA Gear & Maintenance
description: Statement of Work (SOW) SCBA Gear & Maintenance 1.0 Background The Marine Corps Security Force Battalion (MCSFBN) at Naval Base Kitsap-Bangor requires the procurement of Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) kits and associated lifecycle support services to ensure operational readiness for their specialized security mission at Strategic Weapons Facility, Pacific (SWFPAC). To support critical safety operations, respiratory protective equipment must be standardized, certified, and maintained under rigorous Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Mine Safety Appliances (MSA) authorized quality control protocols. 2.0 Scope of Work The contractor shall furnish all personnel, labor, supplies, materials, equipment, technical expertise supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform the work described below in this Statement of Work. This is a firm-fixed-price requirement encompassing a base year (supplies and initial services) and two (2) subsequent option years for recurring maintenance support. 3.0 Technical Specifications & Requirements 3.1 Complete SCBA Kits (CLIN 0001) The contractor shall procure and deliver fifteen (15) complete SCBA kits, brand name Mine Safety Appliances (MSA) G1 Part Number / ATO String: MSA A-G1IN7513H1A1AAH1. Each base kit must meet the following salient characteristics: 4500 psig operating system with a threaded remote cylinder connection. Kevlar harness with padding and a chest strap. Adjustable lumbar pad and a metal cylinder cradle. Left-shoulder continuous hose regulator and remote pressure gauge. Standard Alkaline Battery Power Module (Rechargeable batteries are not required). One (1) 45-Minute, 4500 psig Low-Profile Carbon Cylinder. One (1) Medium facepiece with 4-point Kevlar head harness. One (1) Hard carrying case. Spare Carbon Cylinders (CLIN 0002) The contractor shall procure and deliver fifteen (15) spare carbon-wrapped cylinders, brand name MSA Part Number: MSA 10156424-SP. Salient Characteristics: 45-Minute, 4500 psig Low-Profile carbon-wrapped cylinder equipped for threaded remote connection. Must be natively compatible with the SCBA kits in paragraph 3.1 above. 3.3 Small G1 Facepiece (CLIN 0003) The contractor shall procure and deliver one (1) small facepiece, brand name MSA Part Number MSA 10156458. Salient Characteristics: Must natively match the facepieces bundled in the SCBA kits in paragraph 3.1 above, and feature a 4-point Kevlar head harness, open-port design, and no internal electronics. 3.4 Large G1 Facepieces (CLIN 0004) The contractor shall procure and deliver three (3) large facepieces, brand name MSA Part Number MSA 10156460. Salient Characteristics: Must natively match the facepieces bundled in the SCBA kits in paragraph 3.1 above, and feature a 4-point Kevlar head harness, open-port design, no internal electronics. 4.0 Service Requirements (Base and Option Years) 4.1 Annual SCBA Flow Testing (CLINs 0005, 1001, and 2001) The contractor shall perform preventative maintenance flow tests on each of the fifteen (15) SCBA kits provided in paragraph 3 above once per calendar year in strict accordance with the manufacturer's OEM specifications. This service includes all diagnostic labor, software verification, and technical calibration. Repairs: Any required repairs or replacement parts identified during testing shall be quoted separately to the Government and are not covered under this service CLIN. 4.2 Respiratory Fit Testing (CLINs 0006, 1002, and 2002) The contractor shall perform thirty (30) quantitative respiratory fit tests per period of performance to include fit testing of each SCBA unit twice per calendar year. The contractor shall provide a digital calibration/test report for each SCBA flow test within five (5) business days of testing completion. Fit testing records must be provided immediately upon completion of each test session. The Contractor shall provide all necessary personnel and testing equipment to perform quantitative respiratory fit testing for Government personnel to ensure Occupational Safety and Health Administration/National Fire Protection Association compliance. Frequency: This requirement is intended to be performed for fifteen (15) personnel twice per year (semi-annually). 5.0 Place of Performance Supplies Delivery: All items under CLINs 0001�0004 shall be delivered to SWFPAC, 6403 Skipjack Circle, Silverdale, WA, 98315. Services Execution: The primary place of performance for technical services (CLINs 0005�0006, 1001�1002, and 2001�2002) shall be executed strictly on-site at the Government's facility located at Naval Base Kitsap-Bangor located in Silverdale, WA. The Contractor must have the capability to deploy certified technicians to the on-site Government location to perform all testing, calibration, and fit-testing services. Base Access & Security: For all on-site work, Contractor personnel must strictly comply with all Department of Navy, MCSFBN, and Naval Base Kitsap-Bangor security, badging, and DBIDS clearance protocols. The Contractor is responsible for coordinating all base access requirements with the Government POC at least ten (10) business days in advance of service dates. 6.0 Period of Performance The contractor is required to procure and deliver the items listed in Section 3 above within 60 calendar days from contract award. 7.0 Contractor Furnished Items and Services The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform the work described in this Statement of Work, except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. 8.0 Government Furnished Property None. 9.0 Hours of Operation The contractor is responsible for conducting business between the hours of 7:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. Pacific time Monday thru Friday except Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings. For other than firm fixed price contracts, the contractor will not be reimbursed when the government facility is closed for the above reasons. The contractor must at all times maintain an adequate workforce for the performance of all tasks defined within this statement of work. 10.0 Interchangeability and Standardization All required equipment must be genuine, OEM MSA G1 safety systems. Due to strict military life-safety standards, tactical breaching operational requirements, and a 10-year training baseline established for MCSFBN personnel, alternative manufacturers and non-OEM components are not interchangeable, will not integrate with existing command infrastructure, and will not be accepted for this requirement. 11.0 Special Provisions/Additional Information SECURITY REQUIREMENTS: It is the contractors responsibility to ensure that all contractor personnel can obtain facility access in accordance with Naval Base Kitsap � Bangor facility access requirements. title: **PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE** Forward Based Mode Radar Next Prototype
description: **Pre-Solicitation Notice** The Missile Defense Agency (MDA), Mobile Land-Based Sensors Project Office, is seeking innovative prototype concepts for the Forward-Based Mode (FBM) Radar Next and will solicit this procurement utilizing the existing Missile Defense Agency (MDA) Nimble Options for Buying Layered Effects (NOBLE) Multiple Authority Announcement (MAA). This pre-solicitation is issued under the Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects, pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 4022, to rapidly develop, demonstrate, and evaluate advanced radar prototypes. These systems must be capable of providing enhanced early warning, tracking, and discrimination of emerging missile threats. The primary objective of this effort is to design and prototype a highly mobile, rapidly deployable sensor system. The resulting technology must seamlessly integrate into the existing missile defense architecture to enhance tracking and discrimination capabilities against complex, high-speed, and maneuverable threats, including ballistic, cruise, and hypersonic missiles. To maximize mission success and accelerate the delivery of innovative capabilities, the Government strongly encourages collaborative teaming arrangements that fairly leverage the unique strengths of primes, non-traditional defense contractors (NDCs), and small businesses alike. We believe that diverse, agile partnerships are critical to unlocking novel solutions and driving technological advancement. Accordingly, we seek offerors across all tiers who are prepared to demonstrate a tangible, shared commitment to this effort. We expect proposing entities to bring meaningful resource alignment, co-investment, or shared performance risk to the table, ensuring that the Government and offerors are mutually invested in, and accountable for, the successful execution and long-term outcomes of this program. Offerors will be required to possess or obtain a Facility Security Clearance (FCL) through the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) prior to starting Cycle 1, Concept Development. DD Forms 254 authorizing classified work will be issued to each Offeror no later than the beginning of Cycle 1. **This is not a request for proposal. This notice of Pre-Solicitation does not constitute a solicitation, nor does it constitute a request for proposal, or OT Prototype Proposal. The government is not currently requesting or accepting inquiries or feedback in response to this notice.**
